memberdef.definition: virtual std::vector< GraphGroup > AGRemapCore::GIMIParser< K, V, KeyHash, KeyEqual, ParserBase >::collectParseResult
memberdef.name: collectParseResult

para.verbatim:
embed:rst Collects everything the last #parse produced into the one :cpp:class:`IniGraphGroup` #parse hands back :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` The group holds, in this order: #. every graph in #commandGraphs, under its own ``(component, mod object)`` key #. every graph in #downloadResourceGraphs, under ``(IniGraphModObjKeywords::Download, )`` -- see that class for why the component half is a reserved name. A download whose name is already in the group is skipped, so one resource shared by several registers appears once :raw-html:`
` This is the same group ``GIMIFixer`` builds by hand out of those two members today. :raw-html:`
` .. note:: The graphs in the returned group are **deep copies**, so the group owns them and stays valid however the parser is used afterwards. It has to be: an :cpp:class:`IniGraphGroup` owns its graphs (``std::unique_ptr``), while every graph this parser holds is borrowed from its :cpp:class:`IniParseContext` (see :cpp:class:`IIniGraphGroups`'s ownership contract). ``GIMIFixer`` already deep-copies the command graphs for the same reason -- so a second fixer pass sees the parser's own state unedited :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` The `pybind11`_ layer overrides this to hand back the *live* graph objects in a `Python`_ ``IniGraphGroup`` instead, since a `Python`_ group holds real references rather than owning anything -- see ``PyGIMIParser::parseToPy``

simplesect.para: A one-element vector holding the collected group

memberdef.name: objIdentityKVPs

para.verbatim:
embed:rst ``(mod object) -> the KVPs that IDENTIFY a section for it``, in the order they should be written -- empty for "cannot say" :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` **Only used when this parser has to INVENT a section**, which it does when a mod is missing an object outright and a download has to be hung off something (see :cpp:func:`addDownloads`). A section built from nothing but the download's register is a ``TextureOverride`` with no ``hash``, and a ``TextureOverride`` with no ``hash`` matches no draw call -- so the file is fetched, written, referenced, and never used (for example, a Kirara mod with no face diffuse) :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` Left unset, the invented section carries only the download's register, so a parser that never invents one need not provide it. Set, an EMPTY answer means the object cannot be matched at all, and no section is invented for it -- nor its download declared (CherryHuTao has no face hash, so a mod of hers without a face section used to get a face section with none). :cpp:func:`makeGIMICharParser` supplies it from the same maps its classifier uses, which is the point: the assets that let the classifier RECOGNISE a section are exactly the ones an invented section has to CARRY

para.verbatim:
embed:rst The base of a plain-C++ parser that parses one :cpp:class:`AGRemapCore::IniFile` by its classifiers and a list of steps -- the parser counterpart of :cpp:class:`TemplateFixer` :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` A subclass sets up its classifiers and steps in its constructor. This class supplies what every such parser needs and none of them is about: * the parse context: an :cpp:class:`IniFileParseContext` over the ``.ini`` file, owned here and installed as the parser's context * owning what the parser is built from: its :cpp:class:`GIMISectionClassifier`\\ s (:cpp:func:`ownClassifier`) and its steps (:cpp:func:`addParseStep`, :cpp:func:`addDeferredParseStep`, :cpp:func:`ownStep`), which :cpp:class:`GIMIParser` itself only borrows The steps worth sharing between parsers are edits of their own -- a :cpp:class:`GraphCollect`, a :cpp:class:`ParseDataStep` -- and another ``.ini`` of the mod is read through :cpp:func:`IniFile::sibling`, so a parser built from `Python`_ on the bound :cpp:class:`GIMIParser` has the same pieces
